memos.headline: Relative-strength leaders GOOGL, CAT, AAPL dominate; UNH and PG in structural downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. GOOGL and CAT are the standout momentum names—both up 35-70% over 12-26 weeks, trading within 4% of 52-week highs, and showing massive relative strength vs SPY (+33% and +31% over 12 weeks respectively)—though both are extended at +11-14.5% above their 50-day means, which raises near-term pullback risk. AAPL and JPM offer cleaner risk/reward: both sit near highs with moderate RSI readings (62-64) and positive but not parabolic relative strength. On the other side, UNH is in a severe structural downtrend—48% off its 52-week high, below both moving averages, RSI 32—and PG is similarly weak at -18% drawdown, below both averages with negative relative strength across all timeframes. I would avoid both until they reclaim their 50-day means at minimum.

views.note: Parabolic relative strength (+33% vs SPY 12w) and only -2.1% from highs, but +11% above 50d mean warrants tight stops near 260.
Clean uptrend just -1.1% from 52w high, RSI 63.7 not overbought, positive relative strength; would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~252).
Sitting at virtually new highs (-0.6% drawdown), low ATR of 1.95%, steady relative strength; invalidated below ~306 (50d area).
Extraordinary 12w +35% move with +31% rel strength vs SPY, but +14.5% above 50d mean is the most extended in the universe—position sizing should be small; stop near 500.
Solid 4w +13% rally, +7.5% above 50d mean, RSI 61—constructive but less relative strength than GOOGL/CAT over 12w; stop below 227.
Modest positive trend and mild relative strength, but 26w return of +13.5% lags most leaders; no strong edge either way.
RSI 47.9 is neutral, -9% from highs, and 12w relative strength vs SPY is flat—momentum has stalled despite huge 26w gain; need a close above 200 to get interested.
RSI 33.9 approaching oversold with -8.3% drawdown and negative relative strength across timeframes; could bounce but trend is deteriorating—wait for reclaim of 50d mean (~514).
Persistent downtrend: -18% from highs, below both 50d and 200d means, negative relative strength every timeframe; no reason to step in front of this.
Catastrophic -48% drawdown from 52w high, RSI 32, -15% below 200d mean—this is a broken chart and I see no technical reason to own it until it at least reclaims 345.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Lead on Margin Expansion; UNH Earnings Collapse Demands Caution
memos.body: I see the strongest durable earnings power in NVDA (56.5% net margin, +55.6% YoY revenue growth) and GOOGL (34.2% net margin, +33% YoY net income growth on minimal debt of $14.79B). MSFT continues to compound at 18.4% revenue growth with a 35.7% net margin, though net income growth of 12.5% lags revenue, suggesting cost pressure worth monitoring. UNH is the clear red flag in this universe: net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to just $2.35B on $113B of revenue, compressing net margin to 2.1% while carrying $80.14B in total debt—I need to see medical cost ratios stabilize before getting constructive. XOM's revenue declined 5.2% with net income down 12.3%, reflecting commodity headwinds that may persist, and CAT posted revenue growth of 9.5% but net income fell 6.7%, signaling margin erosion I'd want to see reverse before adding exposure.

views.note: 56.5% net margin and 55.6% YoY revenue growth on only $8.47B total debt represent exceptional earnings power; a sustained margin decline below 45% would change my view.
34.2% net margin with 15.9% revenue growth and 33% net income growth on a clean $14.79B debt load is compelling; I'd reassess if ad revenue growth decelerates below 10%.
18.4% revenue growth and 35.7% net margin are strong, but the gap between revenue and net income growth (12.5%) suggests rising costs that bear watching.
Net margin expanded to 11.8% with net income up 38.2% YoY on $180B revenue, showing operating leverage; I'd turn cautious if margins slip back below 8%.
Revenue grew 7.9% and net income surged 86.4% (likely off a depressed base), but $90.68B in total debt and single-digit top-line growth limit upside conviction.
Solid 31% net margin and 11.6% net income growth, but bank-specific leverage ($427B debt) and macro sensitivity keep me at neutral.
Steady 21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are reassuring for a staple, but 3% revenue growth limits earnings upside.
Net income down 61.2% YoY to $2.35B with net margin collapsing to 2.1% on $80.14B of debt is a clear deterioration in earnings power; I need margin recovery above 5% to reconsider.
Revenue down 5.2% and net income down 12.3% with an 8.8% net margin reflect commodity-driven cash-flow compression I don't want to own into.
Revenue grew 9.5% but net income fell 6.7%, indicating margin pressure at 13%; I'd get constructive if operating margins re-expand above 15%.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal Late-Cycle Caution
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound is now 4.00%, down 100bp over 12 months and 50bp over the last three months, with the effective rate at 4.09% confirming follow-through. However, CPI is running at +3.0% y/y (September print), which is uncomfortably above target and limits the pace of further cuts. Unemployment at 4.40%, up 30bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons, points to a softening labor market that is not yet recessionary but is clearly decelerating. The 10y-2y spread has re-steepened to +54bp from near-flat a year ago, consistent with a mid-cycle easing narrative rather than imminent recession. A regime change call would require either CPI re-accelerating above 3.5% y/y (hawkish pivot risk) or unemployment jumping above 4.8% (recession signal); absent those, I position for moderate easing favoring duration-sensitive quality growth and banks benefiting from a steeper curve, while staying cautious on pure cyclicals exposed to slowing demand.

views.note: Duration-sensitive quality growth benefits from falling front-end rates and a still-positive curve; sticky recurring revenue insulates from mild demand softening.
Easing cycle supports consumer discretionary spending and lowers discount rates on long-duration cash flows, though 3% CPI could pressure margins.
Curve steepening to +54bp from +15bp a year ago directly boosts net interest margins; easing cycle keeps credit losses manageable for now.
Defensive staples offer limited upside in a mid-cycle easing regime; 3% CPI supports pricing power but rate-sensitive bond proxies face competition from still-elevated yields.
Rising unemployment and softening labor market signal cyclical deceleration; CAT's order book is most exposed to capex pullback in a late-cycle slowdown.
Energy is more commodity-driven than macro-driven, but slowing growth and easing policy are not tailwinds; I lack conviction either way without oil price data.
Falling rates reduce discount on high-growth cash flows; secular AI demand partially insulates from cyclical softening, though 3% CPI could slow enterprise budgets.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: AMZN and CAT Surge While MSFT and JPM Face Negative Price Reactions
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available this cycle. AMZN (+9.6%) and CAT (+11.6%) saw outsized positive reactions to their Q3 results filings, suggesting a genuine narrative shift—particularly for CAT, where an industrial name moving double digits on earnings implies the market was positioned too bearishly. MSFT (-2.9%) and JPM (-1.9%) drew negative reactions, and with MSFT's decline coming alongside a prior officer departure filing, the tone around that name feels fragile. AAPL (-0.4%) and XOM (-0.3%) were essentially flat post-earnings, which I read as already-priced stories with no incremental sentiment catalyst. PG's near-zero reaction (+0.2%) and flurry of subsequent 8-K filings (Other Events on 11/3 and 11/4) suggest housekeeping rather than a narrative shift, keeping me neutral there.

views.note: A +9.6% post-earnings move signals a decisive positive sentiment shift that likely has room to carry further in the near term.
An +11.6% earnings-day surge on an industrial name suggests the market was caught offside bearish, creating a positive sentiment inflection.
A -2.9% post-earnings drop combined with a recent officer departure filing points to deteriorating sentiment tone around the name.
A -1.9% earnings reaction followed by routine 8-K filings suggests negative sentiment has not yet found a floor.
A -0.4% post-earnings move is essentially noise; sentiment appears fully priced with no clear directional catalyst.
A +2.5% earnings reaction and a follow-up 8-K on 11/6 suggest modestly positive and still-building sentiment momentum.
A flat +0.2% earnings reaction and multiple routine filings indicate no meaningful sentiment shift in either direction.
A -0.3% post-earnings move is negligible; an officer change filing on 11/3 adds no directional sentiment signal.
A muted +0.5% earnings reaction suggests sentiment is balanced with no strong directional lean.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Falling Oil Signal Geopolitical Crosscurrents for Tech, Energy, and Industrials
memos.body: I see a structurally elevated policy uncertainty environment: the EPU index sits at 316.74, up 38% over three months even as it has ticked down 3% in the last month, suggesting we are on a high plateau rather than in a spike. VIX at 19.50 is up 19% month-over-month and HY OAS has widened 37 bps in a month to 3.13%, confirming that credit and equity vol markets are pricing rising risk premia—consistent with unresolved trade-policy and export-control overhang. WTI crude at $60.24, down nearly 8% over three months, points to demand-side weakness or easing supply fears, which is a headwind for energy but a modest tailwind for cost-sensitive consumer staples and industrials. I have highest conviction that NVDA faces the most concentrated geopolitical risk from potential tightening of semiconductor export controls to China, while PG's defensive profile and global supply-chain diversification make it relatively insulated. A material escalation in US-China chip restrictions or new sanctions would raise my conviction on avoiding NVDA and on favoring PG.

views.note: Semiconductor export-control risk to China remains the single largest geopolitical overhang in the universe; elevated EPU and rising VIX reinforce caution.
Defensive staples with diversified global supply chains benefit from policy uncertainty; multiple recent 8-Ks suggest active investor communication amid volatility.
WTI at $60.24 and falling 8% over 3 months caps upside; geopolitical supply disruption risk provides a floor but demand weakness dominates for now.
Trade-policy uncertainty (EPU +38% 3m) clouds the global capex outlook, but infrastructure spending mandates provide partial offset; staying neutral until tariff clarity emerges.
Cloud and AI revenue streams are less exposed to export-control risk than hardware peers; widening HY spreads favor quality balance sheets.
Positive yield curve slope (10y-2y at +0.54pp) supports NIM, but rising credit spreads and policy uncertainty warrant caution on loan-loss trajectory.
